title: Validate and publish a skill
description: Validate a local SKILL.md, create a skill in Glean, confirm the downloaded file matches your upload, and delete the test skill using the official TypeScript API client.

codeWalkthrough.intro: The example uses the official SDK to validate your file before creating a skill. It retrieves the saved skill, compares the downloaded SKILL.md with the upload, and cleans up afterward. It never extracts files to disk or executes them.

examples.title: Configure the Skills API client
examples.description: Find your Glean instance, obtain credentials through the authentication library, and enable experimental endpoints in the SDK. Node.js loads optional environment settings; the recipe does not parse them itself.

examples.title: Create, retrieve, and delete a test skill
examples.description: Validate the file, create a skill without automatic retries, and retrieve it by the returned ID. Compare downloaded content with the upload, then delete the test skill even if comparison fails. Stop without deleting if the API returns a later version of an existing skill.

examples.title: Compare the stored file with the upload
examples.description: Use yauzl to read the ZIP in memory. Require one regular SKILL.md at the root, bound decompression by the uploaded file size, check its checksum, and compare bytes. Do not compare ZIP bytes: compression and timestamps can differ.

prerequisites: A Glean instance with the experimental Skills Platform APIs enabled
Your work email, or the complete Glean backend HTTPS origin
Permission to create and delete test skills, using OAuth or a user-scoped token with the SKILLS scope.

demoQueries.query: Validate and publish a uniquely named sample skill, then delete the captured ID
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Stdout ends with Verified <name> (<id>) at version 1.0; downloaded <n> byte(s); SKILL.md matches the upload; cleanup completed. The downloaded ZIP must contain one regular root SKILL.md whose checksum and bytes match the upload. Invalid archives or mismatches fail verification and still trigger cleanup. If delete fails, the process exits non-zero, prints the remaining ID and a cleanup command that includes --id, --yes, and the same --email or --server-url used for the run, and does not print that success line.

codeAssets.description: TypeScript CLI that validates a file, creates and retrieves a test skill, compares its downloaded content with the upload, and deletes it afterward

steps.title: Copy the project onto your machine
steps.description: Copy the runnable TypeScript Skills CLI, sample SKILL.md, and credential-free fixture tests into a new directory. OAuth login and secure token storage come from the pinned @gleanwork/auth package.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: Enter the project directory and install its dependencies. Run the remaining commands from this directory.

steps.title: Run the fixture tests
steps.description: Run the tests without credentials or network access. They check the workflow, ZIP content comparison, and failure handling against a fake API. CLI tests block network requests. Passing these tests does not verify access to your Glean instance.

steps.title: Sign in with OAuth
steps.description: Sign in to your Glean instance with the SKILLS scope. The official authentication library handles login and secure credential storage. If OAuth is not available, skip this command: copy .env.example to .env and fill GLEAN_API_TOKEN and GLEAN_SERVER_URL.

steps.title: Choose how to connect to your instance
steps.description: The commands below use OAuth and your work email. With token authentication, omit --email and use GLEAN_SERVER_URL from .env. If email discovery finds the wrong instance, replace --email with --server-url and your complete backend HTTPS origin. If your administrator supplies an OAuth client ID, export GLEAN_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID before login; login does not read .env.

steps.title: Verify against your instance
steps.description: Create a uniquely named test skill, retrieve it, compare the downloaded SKILL.md byte for byte with the upload, and permanently delete it. A mismatch fails verification but still triggers cleanup. Success prints a Verified line ending with cleanup completed. With token authentication, run npm run verify instead of the OAuth command below. Files are not extracted to disk or executed.

steps.title: Test your own SKILL.md
steps.description: The command uses the included sample file. Add --bundle with a path to test your own SKILL.md. Choose an unused name and do not publish that name concurrently. This command also deletes the test skill afterward; it does not leave a published skill for you to use. With token authentication, run npm start -- --yes instead.

questions.prompt: What is your work email address?

architecture.label: Validation
architecture.caption: check the file without saving it

aiPrompt: Scaffold and run the Skills create-and-retrieve quickstart. Ask for the user's work email. Run credential-free fixture tests before authentication. Use the supported SKILLS scope for OAuth and token authentication. Run the official glean-auth CLI directly; do not add a scope-fallback wrapper. Enable experimental APIs through the SDK constructor. Verify with a cryptographically unique SKILL.md: validate it, reject invalid frontmatter without creating anything, create it once without automatic retries, confirm list and get return the captured ID, and verify the downloaded ZIP contains exactly one regular root SKILL.md matching the uploaded bytes. Use yauzl to read the archive in memory, bound decompression by the uploaded file size, and check CRC-32 with node:zlib. Reject malformed archives, unexpected entries, checksum errors, and changed content. A mismatch must still trigger cleanup. Delete the captured ID only when the response identifies a first version. If a later version is returned, stop without deleting it. npm start with no --bundle uses fixtures/sample-skill/SKILL.md; pass --bundle for a different local SKILL.md. Do not put --bundle in the npm start script. npm run verify is the verify subcommand and generates a unique name when --bundle is omitted. If cleanup cannot delete a captured ID, exit non-zero, print the work error, and print the remaining ID plus a cleanup command that includes --id, --yes, and the same --email or --server-url used for the run. Do not publish a second version, do not extract archive files to disk, and do not import from GitHub. Never execute retrieved files or infer cleanup targets from names or catalog search.
llmContext: Use @gleanwork/api-client 0.20.4 with includeExperimental. Validate, create without retries, list, retrieve, and compare the ZIP's single regular root SKILL.md byte-for-byte with the upload. Use yauzl with bounded decompression and node:zlib CRC-32. Reject malformed archives, unexpected entries, bad checksums, and mismatches. Never extract files to disk or execute them. Delete only the captured first-version ID; cleanup failures fail verification. npm run verify generates a unique name. npm start defaults to fixtures/sample-skill/SKILL.md; --bundle overrides it. Name checks are not atomic. Use SKILLS, not skills:read or skills:write. Use official @gleanwork/auth; Node loads .env. Version management and GitHub import are out of scope.

content.problem: You have a local SKILL.md file and want to publish it to your Glean instance. Before adding version management or GitHub imports, start by validating the file, creating a skill, and checking that you can retrieve it. This quickstart uses the official TypeScript API client to complete that workflow, then deletes the test skill. It verifies that the downloaded SKILL.md matches the uploaded file byte for byte, without extracting files to disk or executing the skill.
takeItFurther: Use the skill-publishing-pipeline recipe to publish another version, inspect a specific version, and examine a downloaded archive safely.
Use the GitHub import recipe when the source of truth is a public repository rather than a local SKILL.md.
After you can create and retrieve a skill, use its ID to explore version management and enabling or disabling it.

guardrails.title: Validate before creating a skill
guardrails.rule: Call validate first and stop on any error. Validation itself never creates or updates a skill.

guardrails.title: Use a new name
guardrails.rule: The API can add a version when a name already exists. Use an unused name and avoid concurrent runs with that name. Creation is not retried automatically. If creation times out, inspect your instance before running it again; a skill may have been saved without returning its ID.

guardrails.title: Treat content as untrusted
guardrails.rule: Limit the ZIP download to 10 MiB. Read its single regular root SKILL.md in memory, with decompression bounded by the uploaded file size. Require a valid checksum and exact file bytes. Do not extract files to disk or execute retrieved content.

guardrails.title: Delete by captured ID only
guardrails.rule: Deletion is permanent. Clean up only the new skill identified by the create response, never a name-search result. If the API returns a later version, stop without deleting it. If deletion fails, the command reports the remaining ID and exits with an error.

limitations.title: Experimental API
limitations.description: The scaffold opts in with includeExperimental, but the Skills endpoints may still be unavailable on a tenant or change before general availability.

limitations.title: Publishing is not execution
limitations.description: The API stores and distributes skill bundles. This quickstart verifies the bytes of a single uploaded SKILL.md, not multi-file bundles or skill execution. It does not run the skill or test how an agent host interprets it.

limitations.title: Sign-in permissions vary by instance
limitations.description: Your instance must allow the SKILLS scope. If OAuth is unavailable, use a user-scoped token with that scope. The newer skills:read and skills:write scopes are not supported yet.
